questions.q: A director wants the audience to feel a tycoon's power growing. Which camera choice is the conventional tool?
choices: A high angle looking down at him
A low angle looking up at him
questions.explain: Low angles tend to make characters look strong or monumental, as with Kane.

questions.q: A film opens with a long shot through a masked figure's eyes as they enter a house and kill. What's the technique, and its effect?
choices: Subjective camera: it makes the audience share the killer's eyes
Deep focus: it keeps everyone sharp
An establishing shot: it orients us
questions.explain: As in the opening of Halloween, the camera becomes the character.

questions.q: Why is Lady in the Lake, shot almost entirely from the hero's point of view, usually judged a failure?
choices: We never see the hero's face, so we lose the reactions that build sympathy
questions.explain: Living permanently in someone's eyes removes the face, and with it the reaction shot.

questions.q: In one frame, a mother signs papers in the foreground while her son plays in the snow, sharp, through the window. What's the technique?
questions.explain: Deep focus keeps near and far sharp so the composition makes the connection without a cut.

questions.q: A screenwriter wants the audience to feel a character's loneliness in a new city without dialogue. Which written image best implies the right shot?
choices: Close on her lips as she speaks
Far below, she stands alone on an empty platform as the train pulls away
A jump cut to her hotel room
questions.explain: Wide shots set people small in their surroundings; distance reads as isolation.

questions.q: Why might a director stage a nightclub entrance as one unbroken Steadicam shot rather than in cuts?
choices: Because long takes are cheaper to edit
Because the continuous movement itself conveys the character's access and the seduction of that world
questions.explain: In Goodfellas's Copacabana shot, the unbroken path through the kitchen is the meaning.

questions.q: A playwright wants the audience to watch one silent character during a crowded party scene. Without a close-up, what can she do?
choices: Use blocking, levels, light or other characters' looks to direct focus
Nothing: stage audiences can't be directed
questions.explain: Theatre is a permanent wide shot, so focus is directed by staging.

ideas: Which approach treats the distance between camera and face as the distance between audience and feeling?
Which approach keeps foreground and background sharp at once so the viewer finds the connection without a cut?
Which approach holds a single moving shot for minutes so that continuous time and space become the meaning?
Which approach tilts the horizon to signal that the world of the story is off balance?
